## 3.3 Finance

## Efficiency investment is resilient and projected to reach about USD 660 billion in 2024

Combined public and private investment in end-use sectors on efficiency, including electrification, is set to increase slightly by nearly 4% in 2024, matching is around 10% more than all upstream oil and gas investment in 2024. Investment has risen by a strong 45% since 2019, as the energy crisis and Covid-19 pandemic prompted massive government spending to stimulate consumer investment in estimated 77%, followed by 34% for buildings and 13% in industry.

More recently, investment trends have been more mixed. Between 2022 and 2024, investment is estimated to have declined by 7% in the buildings sector and on efficient electrification is rising rapidly, primarily through EVs in China, Europe declining from recent highs as the effects of high energy prices ease and Covid-19 stimulus spending winds down.As a result, overall global end-use investment has plateaued over the last two years, with higher inflation and interest rates making it
